Other carbons: 52.24 (likely O-CH3 or O-CH2), 43.47 (maybe CH2 attached to carbonyl), 38.60 (maybe CH3). So total carbons: 6 aromatic + 3 aliphatic + 1 carbonyl = 10? So C10H12O.

Our formula C11H14O2 suggests maybe a phenyl ring with an ester group attached (C=O-O-alkyl) plus an extra carbon elsewhere. For example, methyl 4-phenylbutanoate: phenyl-CH2-CH2-CH2-COOCH3? That's C11H14O2? Let's count: phenyl C6H5, three CH2 (C3H6), carbonyl C (C1O1), OCH3 (C1H3O1). Total C11 (6+3+1+1), H5+6+3=14, O2. Yes matches formula. So methyl 4-phenylbutanoate (also called methyl phenylbutyrate). That would have carbonyl at one end, OCH3 (52 ppm), CH2 next to carbonyl (43 ppm), CH2 further (38.6 maybe), aromatic carbons as observed. The carbonyl carbon at 166 ppm matches ester carbonyl. The OCH3 carbon at ~52 ppm matches. The CH2 adjacent to carbonyl (alpha) around 43 ppm, the next CH2 around 38.6 ppm. Aromatic carbons: ipso carbon attached to chain maybe 131.9, ortho/meta/para around 129. So this fits.

Thus SMILES: CCOC(=O)CCCC? Wait methyl phenylbutanoate: structure: phenyl-CH2-CH2-CH2-COOCH3. SMILES: "COC(=O)CCCc1ccccc1"? Need correct order: methyl ester of 4-phenylbutanoic acid: O=C(OCH3)CCCC? Here we have phenyl substituting at the terminal carbon (the CH3 replaced by phenyl). So chain: phenyl-CH2-CH2-CH2-COOCH3. Yes.
